correctness.rationale: Exact odd/even splitting forces d congruent n modulo 4 and gives p((n-d)/4) q((n+d)/2). The two classical partition asymptotics give the central saddle C sqrt(n) and quadratic decrement -C d^2/(8 n^(3/2)); the prefactor is 2^(3/4)/3^(1/4) n^(-3/4). Concavity globally bounds the residual mass and yields all fixed moment convergence, so variance tends to (2 sqrt 6/pi)n^(3/2). Exact independent enumerations through n=22 and exact fiber-mass checks through n=200 were run with packaged verifier. Finite checks do not prove the asymptotic.

originality.rationale: The aggregate SOME(n) generating function and congruences are prior results, and the splitting bijection is elementary; novelty is only the lattice-normal law, sharp variance and balanced-atom asymptotic. Inspected original and 2026 follow-up, distinct-index alternating statistic, part-count arithmetic-progression limits, and restricted aggregate results. No inspected statement implies the claimed lattice local law for parity-weighted total mass, though general local central limit frameworks may cover it and historical priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: A general uninspected local-limit theorem for additive linear statistics of random partitions might imply the Gaussian assertion and thereby limit originality.
Earlier unindexed studies of signed mass by part-value parity may exist; negative searches do not prove uniqueness.

value.rationale: The recent arithmetic function SOME(n) aggregates signed odd/even part-size mass but obscures the individual-partition distribution. The new lattice-local Gaussian statement identifies exact fluctuations, full finite fibers, the sharp variance coefficient, and the density of perfect balance, including a forced mod-4 obstruction. This is a motivated classification and distributional theorem rather than a routine substitution or table recomputation.
